findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancellation permanently blocks all future cancellations
findings.body: The whole cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls are collected as lazy Prisma promises that are only executed by `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop finishes. If any `client.request` call throws (SendGrid rejects a cancellation that is less than ~10 minutes before `sendAt`, or returns 400 because the batch already has a `cancel` status), the loop aborts and *none* of the already-cancelled reminders are deleted from the DB. On the next cron run the same rows are re-processed; the previously-cancelled batches now return an error themselves, so the run aborts again. The result is a poisoned queue in which no reminder is ever cancelled or removed — exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix. The failure is also only `console.log`ged and the endpoint still returns HTTP 200, so it is invisible to monitoring. Each reminder should be cancelled and deleted independently with its own try/catch.

findings.title: Reschedule path still cancels at SendGrid immediately, so rescheduled bookings are not fixed
findings.body: For rescheduled bookings the old reminders are cancelled with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, i.e. `immediateDelete = true`, which performs the direct `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` call. That is precisely the call that silently fails once SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit is reached (the root cause described in the PR). Because the `cancelled` flag is not set and the reminder row is not deleted in that branch, the CRON job will never retry the cancellation, so the reminder email for the old (rescheduled-away) booking is still delivered. The PR title claims to fix rescheduled bookings, but this path bypasses the new deferred-cancellation mechanism entirely.

findings.title: immediateDelete branch cancels at SendGrid but never deletes the reminder row
findings.body: In the `immediateDelete` branch the function returns right after the SendGrid cancel request, without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row and without setting `cancelled`. Callers that rely on the function to clean up (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts`, where the original booking is kept) leave behind rows with `scheduled: true` and a stale `referenceId` pointing at a cancelled batch. These rows only disappear when the CRON's `deleteMany` eventually removes reminders whose `scheduledDate` has passed, and in the meantime there is no record that the cancellation needs retrying if the SendGrid request failed. The function name (`delete...`) and the other two branches (delete row / flag row) make this inconsistency a correctness problem, not just cosmetics.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are no longer awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are invoked inside `forEach` without `await` (the previous code collected the Prisma promises and awaited them in `Promise.all`). Nothing in the handler guarantees these DB writes (setting `cancelled: true`, deleting SMS reminder rows, Twilio cancellations) complete before the request returns. In a serverless deployment the execution context can be frozen as soon as the handler resolves, so the reminder may never be flagged as cancelled and the workflow email will still be sent — the exact bug being fixed. The same pattern was introduced in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`; in the latter the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch anything either because the promise is not awaited.

findings.title: Workflow/step deletion still relies on immediate SendGrid cancellation with no retry possible
findings.body: When a workflow is deleted (line 214) or a step is removed (line 521), reminders are cancelled with `immediateDelete = true` and immediately afterwards the workflow/step is deleted, which cascade-deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows. If the direct `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` call fails — the failure mode this PR addresses, and failures are only `console.log`ged — the scheduled emails are still delivered and the DB record needed to retry the cancellation is gone. Deleting a workflow with many upcoming reminders can also exceed SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit in one burst, reintroducing the original bug for this path.

findings.title: remindersToCancel query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders with a referenceId
findings.body: The query selects every `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled: true`, without filtering on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or on a non-null `referenceId`, and then posts `reminder.referenceId` as a SendGrid `batch_id`. Today only email reminders ever get the flag, but any row that is flagged with a Twilio SID or a null reference (now or after a future change) will produce a SendGrid 400 which, given the shared try/catch, aborts the whole cancellation batch (see the loop issue). Add the method/referenceId filters to make the query match the intent stated in the comment.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import and malformed import formatting
findings.body: The import list was changed to a value import that now includes `Prisma`, but after removing the `Prisma.BatchPayload` usages `Prisma` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file, so this is an unused import that will trip `no-unused-vars` in CI. The entry also lacks the trailing comma (`TimeUnit,\n  Prisma\n}`), which prettier will flag. Both will fail the lint/format check.

findings.title: New cron query on `cancelled`/`scheduledDate` has no supporting index
findings.body: The migration adds `cancelled BOOLEAN` with no default and no index, while the cron now runs `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` every 15 minutes against `WorkflowReminder`, a table that grows with every booking. With no index on (`cancelled`, `scheduledDate`) this is a full table scan on each run. Making the column `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (and the Prisma field `Boolean @default(false)`) would also avoid the three-state null/false/true semantics that every future query has to account for.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new deferred cancellation flow
findings.body: The fix introduces a new state machine (flag `cancelled` on cancel/reschedule → cron cancels at SendGrid within one hour → delete row) spread across the cancel handler, the reschedule handler, the workflow router and this cron endpoint, but no test is added. Given that the previous attempt at this fix (#6991) shipped broken and silently stopped cancelling emails, at least a unit test for `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (each of the three branches) and for the cron's cancellation loop (including a failing SendGrid request not blocking the remaining reminders) would prevent another silent regression.
